rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading makes then he says accusative, treating it as coordinated with the preceding construction; Abu Amr reads it nominative as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ثم يقول بنصب اللام، وروي عن أبي عمرو برفعها، أما النصب فعلى تقدير لا تجتمع النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most named readers use the light form of teach, while the remaining readers use the doubled form, which he says conveys more benefit by combining knowledge and teaching.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب تعلمون بالتخفيف من علم يعلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb with an open tāʾ and ʿayn and a doubled lām, meaning they learn.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن بفتح التاء والعين وتشديد اللام في معنى يتعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads يدرسون with a damma on yāʾ and no doubling; Saʿid b. Jubayr reads تدرسون as teaching, while the common reading is the light form from درس.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي حيوة يدرسون بضم الياء والتخفيف من درس يدرس، وعن سعيد بن جبير تدرسون من التدريس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers put ولا يأمركم in the accusative, coordinating it with the construction governed by أن or with ثم يقول; the others use nominative as a fresh clause after the sentence ends.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة وابن عامر ويعقوب ولا يأمركم بنصب الراء عطفا على ما عملت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar derives from skin and names the visibly embodied human; like خلق, it can denote either one person or a group.
rows.anchor: البشر من البشرة سمي بذلك لظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation of rabbānī is from rabbān, a manager who orders and reforms people's affairs; a scholar is called rabbānī because knowledge lets him govern affairs.
rows.anchor: وهو من يرب أمر الناس بتقديره لهم وإصلاحه إياه رب أمره يربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second derivation links rabbānī to the Lord and His religious knowledge, expressed through a relational form like Najrānī or Liḥyānī.
rows.anchor: وهو علم الدين الذي أمر به إلا أنه عبر بالإضافة

rows.speaker: بعض قريش
rows.claim: A Qurayshi saying illustrates rabbānī as managing or raising someone: the speaker would rather be managed by a Qurayshi than a man from Hawazin.
rows.anchor: قول بعض قريش: لأن يربني رجل من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant forms of كأين are recognized Arabic dialects, but he prefers the Qurayshi form because it was the Prophet's language and the Qur'an's language, and most readers use it.
rows.anchor: كلها لغات معروفة، والاختيار لغة قريش؛ لأنها لغة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and others read قتل without an alif, ascribed to Ibn Abbas; the other reading قاتل with an alif is ascribed to Ibn Masud, distinguishing survivors from those named.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب قتل بضم القاف وكسر التاء بغير ألف، وهي قراءة ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading قاتل with an alif, attributed to Ibn Masud, places the denial of weakness on the ones mentioned in the battle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون قاتل بالألف، وهي قراءة ابن مسعود، ففي الأول نفي الوهن عمن بقي، وفي الثاني عمن ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has kasra on the first letter of ربيون; Ibn Masud reads it with damma, a Tamimi dialect.
rows.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ربيون بكسر الراء، وهي اللغة العالية، وعن ابن مسعود بضم الراء، وهي لغة تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read وهنوا with a fatḥa; Abu al-Simal uses kasra, explained by al-Mubarrad, Abu Hatim, and al-Kisai through different verb patterns.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو [السمال] العدوي بكسر الهاء، أما الفتح فهو وهن يهن وهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كأين originates from أي with the comparative kaf added, as كذا comes from ذا with kaf; its sound changed as its meaning shifted to كم.
rows.anchor: أصل (كأين): (أي) دخلت عليها كاف التشبيه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The word for the many devout companions is said to mean a group; its plural ربيون derives from ربوة, and another view gives ربي as its singular.
rows.anchor: وجمع الربة الربيون، عن أبي علي وجماعة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another derivation relates the word to the Lord, with a kasra in its first syllable as in other relational forms.
rows.anchor: بناء رباني كديراني ينسب إلى الدير، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris defines a ربي as one who is devout and knows the Lord.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس: الربي المتأله العارف بالرب

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Istikāna means submission and humility; miskīn is connected to this lowly state, and the verb derives from stillness, with an underlying استكونوا.
rows.anchor: التذلل والخضوع، عن أبي مسلم، ومنه أخذ المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage refutes the Compulsionists' doctrine about created acts: the injury comes from disbelievers and believers are commanded to endure it; otherwise the command would make no sense.
rows.anchor: من جهة الكفار، وأمرهم بالصبر، ولو كان الجميع خلقا له لم يكن للكلام معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Abu Amr read both verbs in the third person, referring to the People of the Book; the others address them directly.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو ليبيننه ولا يكتمونه بالياء فيهما كناية عن أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mīthāq is rooted in mutual assurance and originally means making something firm.
rows.anchor: الميثاق من المواثقة وأصله الإحكام، وثقت الشيء أحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means throwing away; warāʾ is the opposite of before; ishtarā derives from shira and can be used whether or not money or goods are exchanged.
rows.anchor: يقال نبذت الشيء من يدي إذا ألقيته من يدك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The pronoun in لتبيننه can refer to Muhammad, understood though not previously named.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير والسدي، فتعود على معلوم غير مذكور

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The pronoun in لتبيننه can instead refer to the Book; explaining it includes explaining the Prophet because the Book contains his matter.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة، فيدخل فيه بيان أمر النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وإذ is governed by an omitted command, estimated as remember, O Messenger, when God took the covenant.
rows.anchor: قلنا: المحذوف تقديره: واذكر إذ أخذ الله

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim construes the clause as referring to the People of the Book casting behind them the covenant they had received.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: وتقدير الكلام: وإذ نبذ أهل الكتاب وراء ظهورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لتبيننه is emphatic and enters an oath; the implied demand is that they swear they will explain it.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: لتبيننه لام التأكيد ويدخل على اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account links the breach to the wicked acts just mentioned; another follows the warning that they may call the Messenger a liar despite a reinforced covenant.
rows.anchor: قيل: حكى عنهم نقض الميثاق كما حكى فيما تقدم أفعالهم الخبيثة، وقيل: لما تقدم فإن كذبوك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: One view says prophets took an oath from their communities to disclose Muhammad's mission to people.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو اليمين الذي أخذها الأنبياء على أممهم ليبينوا أمر محمد للناس عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies those who received the covenant as the Jews.
rows.anchor: قيل: اليهود عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والسدي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes both Jews and Christians among the People of the Book addressed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اليهود والنصارى عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: A broader interpretation includes everyone given knowledge of any divine book, who must disclose it and not conceal it.
rows.anchor: لتبيننه ولا تكتمه عن محمد بن كعب والحسن وقتادة والأصم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When al-Hajjaj challenged al-Hasan over his criticism of growing hypocrisy, al-Hasan answered that the covenant to disclose truth compelled him to speak.
rows.anchor: قال الأصم: ذكروا أن الحجاج قال للحسن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud tells Kaʿb to return the greeting and says the verse was revealed while Kaʿb was still Jewish, rejecting the claim that it did not concern him.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود: أقرئه السلام وأخبره أنها نزلت وهو يهودي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Shaʿbi say the People of the Book left the covenant unpracticed even while continuing to recite it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والشعبي: تركوا العمل به وكانوا يقرؤونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to conceal means they must not hide the matter when disclosure is needed.
rows.anchor: أي لا تخفونه عند الحاجة فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم أي طرحوه خلف ظهورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says they hid Muhammad's description, professed Judaism, and took a small payment from followers and common people.
rows.anchor: وأظهروا اليهودية وأخذوا عليه شيئا يسيرا من أتباعهم وعوامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says they abandoned Islam to preserve leadership they feared losing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تركوا الإسلام لرئاسة لهم خافوا زوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says they accepted bribes, altered rulings, and issued unjust opinions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أخذوا الرشوة وغيروا الأحكام وأفتوا بغير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad bargain is their abandonment of the covenant for payment; another interpretation says the price is earning permanent punishment.
rows.anchor: أن يستحقوا به العقاب الدائم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires publicizing truth and forbids concealment, including matters of religion, law, legal opinions, and testimony.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على وجوب إظهار الحق وتحريم كتمانه، فيدخل فيه بيان الدين والأحكام والفتاوى والشهادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book possess information known through them, possibly the Prophet's description or legal matters known only to scholars.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن هناك أمورا يختص لمعرفتها أهل الكتاب ويعلم ذلك من جهتهم، وهو يحتمل بيان صفة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns those who abandon Scripture for worldly gain.
rows.anchor: وتدل على ذم من يترك الكتاب لدنيا يصيبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read the first verb in the third person; Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai address the listener directly.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: لا يحسبن الذين يفرحون بالياء وفتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the second prohibition, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr use a third-person form, while the remaining readers address the listener; in both readings the object is accusative.
rows.anchor: فلا تحسبنهم الثاني: بالياء وضم الباء ابن كثير وأبو عمرو على تقدير:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading أتوا means they did; Ibrahim lengthens it as آتوا, while Saʿid b. Jubayr reads passive أوتوا, meaning they were given.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: أتوا وعن إبراهيم آتوا بالمد. أي أعطوا من أنفسهم، وعن سعيد بن جبير أوتوا أعطوا على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farah and marah are near-synonyms for being exhilarated by good news, a blameworthy trait that Arabs prided themselves on avoiding.
rows.anchor: الفرح والمرح من النظائر، وهو أن يستفز حال البشارة صاحبها وذلك مذموم عند العرب يتمادحون بتركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line depicts someone who neither rejoices at fortune nor despairs at events, supporting the praised restraint.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: فلا فرح إن أتاه ... ولا جزع من الحدثان لاعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also uses being exceedingly joyful and boastful as blameworthy language.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى: (إنه لفرح فخور)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most explain مفازة as escape or salvation; Abu Muslim instead glosses it as distance.
rows.anchor: والمفازة والنجاة والخلاص واحد وهو الفوز، يقول: فاز يفوز فوزا ومفازة أي تخلص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explicitly links the description of the joyful and boastful person to Qur'an 10:10.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى: (إنه لفرح فخور)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate of the first لا تحسبن has two analyses: it is بمفازة من العذاب, with the fāʾ possibly extra; or it is omitted and understood from the later predicate.
rows.anchor: قلنا: فيه قولان: الأول: خبرها (بمفازة من العذاب)؛ لأنها مكسورة لطول الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion says the verse concerns hypocrites who skipped the Prophet's campaigns, then made excuses and wanted praise for faith they lacked.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في أهل النفاق؛ لأنهم كانوا يجتمعون على التخلف عن الجهاد

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The hypocrite occasion report is transmitted from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, Rafiʿ b. Khadij, Zayd b. Thabit, and Ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري ورافع بن خديج وزيد بن ثابت وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another occasion concerns People of the Book, who rejoiced at jointly denying the Prophet and concealing his message, wanting praise for piety and learning they lacked.
rows.anchor: فأحبوا أن يحمدوا بما ليس فيهم من أنهم أهل نسك وعلم عن ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews of Medina reportedly wrote to distant communities that Muhammad was no messenger, then rejoiced in their unity and claimed knowledge and Abraham's religion.
rows.anchor: وروي أن يهود المدينة كتبوا إلى أطراف الأرض بأن محمدا ليس برسول فاثبتوا على دينكم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says it was revealed about Phinehas and Jewish rabbis who rejoiced in misleading people while falsely claiming to be learned leaders.
rows.anchor: وقولهم: إنهم علماء وأئمة وليسوا كذلك عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Jews rejoiced that people admired their alteration of Scripture and praised them for it.
rows.anchor: بتبديلهم الكتاب وحمدهم إياهم عليه عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Jews of Khaybar falsely told the Prophet they recognized and believed him; Muslims praised them, prompting this revelation. Al-Asamm reports a similar account.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية فيهم عن قتادة. وعن الأصم قريبا منه.

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports that the verse concerned Jews who equipped and funded an army against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: جهزوا جيشا إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأنفقوا عليهم عن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas rejects applying the threat to everyone who is pleased with their deeds: the verse concerns People of the Book who concealed an answer from the Prophet and rejoiced in that concealment.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ما لكم ولهذه الآية، إنما نزلت في أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Medinan; its verse count differs by region: 176 in Kufa, 175 in the Hijaz and Basra, and 177 in Syria.
rows.anchor: وهي مدنية. مائة وست وسبعون آية في الكوفي، وخمس في الحجازي والبصري

rows.speaker: ابن كعب
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Kaʿb says the Prophet promised a reader of Surat al-Nisa reward like charity to every believer, an inheritance, freeing a person, and deliverance from associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كعب عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: من قرأ سورة النساء فكأنما تصدق على كل مؤمن ومؤمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior surah ended with a command to fear God, and this one opens with the same command, extending obedience across both surahs.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم السورة المتقدمة بالأمر بالتقوى افتتح هذه السورة بالأمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the transition is that the former surah addressed believers, while this opening commands all morally responsible people to fear God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمر هناك بالتقوى للمؤمنين وأمر ههنا لجميع المكلفين بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read تساءلون with a light sīn by deleting a tāʾ; others double the sīn through assimilation.
rows.anchor: قرأ تساءلون بتخفيف السين عاصم وحمزة والكسائي، والباقون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza alone, with al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, and al-Aʿmash, reads الأرحام in the genitive; the others read it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحده والأرحام بخفض الميم، وهي قراءة النخعي وقتادة والأعمش، وقرأ الباقون بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the fatḥa: it means fear severing kinship ties, and Arabic normally avoids coordinating an explicit noun with a preposition attached to a pronoun unless repeating the preposition.
rows.anchor: فوجه ذلك: واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet supplies a rare precedent for coordinating an explicit noun with a preposition attached to a pronoun.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: فاليوم أصبحت تهجونا وتشتمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read الأرحام nominative as a new subject after ending the previous clause; al-Akhfash says the genitive reading implies an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم والأرحام بالرفع على الابتداء، كأنه نوى تمام الكلام عند قوله: تساءلون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce qāf and kāf distinctly in خلقكم; some assimilate qāf into kāf because they share an articulation point.
rows.anchor: والقراء على إظهار القاف والكاف في قوله: خلقكم ومنهم من يدغم القاف في الكاف؛ لأنه من مخرجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has اللاتي with tāʾ; Ibn Masud reads اللائي without tāʾ, as in Qur'an 65:4.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود: اللائي أرضعنكم: بغير تاء كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمهات is a plural of أم; one derivation has an original hāʾ that disappears in the singular and returns in the plural, while another gives أمه as the root and أمات as its plural.
rows.anchor: الأمهات: جمع أم، والأم في الأصل أمهة على وزن فعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line preserves the hāʾ in أمهتي, supporting the proposed original form.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: أمهتي خندف وإلياس أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rabība is a man's stepdaughter, called that because he raises her; the word has the sense of the passive مربوبة.
rows.anchor: والربيبة: بنت امرأة الرجل من غيره وقيل لها ربيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥalīla is a son's wife; one derivation says spouses are mutually lawful for intercourse, with حليل formed like صحيح.
rows.anchor: والحلائل: أزواج الابن، والذكر حليل، وجمعه أحلة كأعزة وأعزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation says spouses are called ḥalīl and ḥalīla because they share a bed, from the sense of dwelling or lodging.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنها يحل معها في فراش من الحلول، وهو النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase وأن تجمعوا is nominative by estimation: it is forbidden to combine the two sisters; ما is an accusative exception for what occurred before the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وأن تجمعوا محله رفع على تقدير: وحرم الجمع إلا ما قد سلف. قوله: ما في محل النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first اللاتي is nominative as an adjective of ربائبكم, and the second is genitive as an adjective of النساء.
rows.anchor: اللاتي محله رفع نعتا لربائبكم، واللاتي الثاني محله خفض نعتا للنساء

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the rule on sons' wives was revealed when the Prophet married Zayd b. Haritha's former wife; the polytheists criticized him, and Qur'an 33:4 and 33:40 also came down.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: نزل قوله: وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation account also links this passage to the declaration that adopted sons are not biological sons and Muhammad is not the father of any adult man.
rows.anchor: ونزل: (وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم) و(ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is both judge and messenger, though one may be a messenger without being a judge or a judge without being a messenger; combining the roles honors him.
rows.anchor: رسول ليس بحاكم وحاكم ليس برسول، فجمع له الأمرين تشريفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's judgment is binding, whether it institutes law or resolves a case referred to him.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن قضاءه لازم؛ لأنه إما أن يكون ابتداء شرع فيلزم، أو يحكم بعد الرفع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting the Messenger is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الرد على الرسول كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Submission is insufficient without inward compliance and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن التسليم لا يغني ما لم ينضم إليه انقياد القلب والإخلاص

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer from the verse that the Prophet's commands are obligatory; al-Qadi rejects this inference because binding judgments differ from commands.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بالآية على أن أوامره على الوجوب، قال القاضي: الظاهر أن قضاءه لازم، والقضاء هو الإلزام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Ubayy b. Kaʿb, and Isa b. Umar read قليلا in the accusative; others read it nominative, matching their codices.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبي بن كعب وعيسى بن عمر قليلا بالنصب، وكذا هو في مصاحف الشام، ومصحف أنس بن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading either makes the few the subject of فعلوه or restarts the clause as an explanatory exception; the accusative is an exception or an implied phrase.
rows.anchor: فأما الرفع فعلى ضمير الفاعل من قوله: فعلوه تقديره: فعله القليل، وقيل: على التكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in the vowels of أن اقتلوا and أو اخرجوا: three combinations are reported, with each reader group and phonetic explanation specified.
rows.anchor: في قوله: (أن اقتلوا) - (أو اخرجوا) ثلاث قراءات: الأول: بضم نون (أن)، وواو (أو)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتب means prescribed or imposed, as in the prescription of fasting, and its root sense is writing.
rows.anchor: كتب: فرض، ومنه: (كتب عليكم الصيام) وأصله من الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تثبيت is the verbal noun on tafʿīl from steadfastness; a steadfast warrior remains standing and is not thrown down.
rows.anchor: تثبيت: تفعيل من ثبت الشيء ثباتا، ورجل ثبت في الحرب، وثبت إذا لم يزل ولم يصرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persisting in worship increases a person's firmness and peace of mind because God gives him subtle support.
rows.anchor:
له.
ويدل قوله: ولهديناهم أن الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to guide them shows that guidance can lead to Paradise and reward, against the Compulsionists' claim that God creates faith.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: ولهديناهم أن الهدى قد يكون إلى الجنة وإلى الثواب خلاف قول المجبرة: إنه خلق الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq may mean one who consistently fulfills what belief in truth requires, or someone habitually truthful; its root contrasts with lying.
rows.anchor: الصديق: المداوم على ما يوجبه التصديق بالحق، وقيل: الصديق الذي عادته الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ṣiddīq can describe one who habitually does an action, with analogies for habitual drinking, drunkenness, or wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وكل من غلب على عادته فعل، فإذا وصف به نبي جاء على فعيل من ذلك الفعل، يقال للملازم الخمر خمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr is called al-Siddiq because he never denied the Prophet; Ali also called himself the greatest ṣiddīq for the same reason.
rows.anchor: ومنه سمي أبو بكر صديقا، وعن علي (عليه السلام): (أنا الصديق الأكبر)؛ لأنهما لم يكذبا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq may inflect as a noun and take dual or plural forms, or remain unchanged like verbal nouns such as زفير and شهيق.
rows.anchor: والصديق قد يثنى ويجمع فيذهب بها إلى أنه اسم، وقد لا يثنى ولا يجمع؛ لأنه يشبه المصدر نحو: (زفير وشهيق)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Martyrs are named because they testify to the truth until killed, or because they belong among the witnesses of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والشهداء: جمع شهيد، وسمي شهيدا؛ لأنه أقام شهادة الحق حتى قتل، وقيل: لأنه من شهداء الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafīq means companion, from treating an activity gently; a traveling party is called رفقة because its members assist one another.
rows.anchor: والرفيق: الصاحب وأصله من الرفق في العمل، وهو الارتفاق فيه، ومنه الرفقة الجماعة في السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رفيقا is accusative either as specification or circumstantial description; its singular form is explained by either analysis or by treating each person as a companion.
rows.anchor: نصب رفيقا قيل: على التمييز، تقديره: حسن أولئك رفيقا، وقيل: على الحال، وفي توحيد (رفيقا) قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line uses صديق in the singular as a predicate-like description of plural women, illustrating the grammar.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: نصبن الهوى ثم ارتمين قلوبنا ... بأعين أعداء وهن صديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in كفى بالله is called extra for emphasis, yielding God suffices; another reading says the servants are content with God.
rows.anchor: ودخل الباء في كفى بالله قيل: زائدة تأكيدا، وتقديره كفى الله، وقيل: معناه اكتفى العباد بالله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A man tells the Prophet he loves him more than himself and family, cannot bear separation, and fears not seeing him in Paradise because the Prophet will be with the prophets; Gabriel then brings the verse.
rows.anchor: روى قاضي القضاة عماد الدين رحمة الله عليه بإسناده عن الأسود عن عائشة أن رجلا جاء إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says the Prophet is raised among the prophets in Paradise, which the man fears will separate them after death.
rows.anchor: وإذا ذكرت الموت عرفت أنك في الجنة ترفع مع النبيين وإني إذا دخلت الجنة لا أراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise God gives believers refutes the claim that they are compelled to obey without choice.
rows.anchor: لأن مدحهم وما وصفهم تعالى به في القرآن لا يليق بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides the reward and then grants more than what was deserved; increasing deserved punishment would be injustice, whereas reward beyond entitlement is grace.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه تعالى يوفر الثواب ثم يزيدهم على ما استحقوا، وأنه لا يزيدهم على العقاب المستحق؛ لأنه ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward and punishment occur after the resurrection.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الثواب والعقاب يكون بعد الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward and punishment repay deeds, contrary to the Compulsionists' position.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الثواب والعقاب جزاء على الأعمال خلاف ما يقوله أهل الجبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human acts originate from human agents, refuting the claim that they are created by God in the way the Compulsionists assert.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن أفعال العباد حادثة من جهتهم، فيبطل قولهم في المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Burhān means a witness that is true in itself or a clear proof; the verb برهن means to establish something by evidence.
rows.anchor: البرهان: الشاهد بالحق في نفسه، وقيل: البرهان: البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase برهانان من ربك refers to two proofs.
rows.anchor: ومنه: (برهانان من ربك) أي: حجتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtiṣām means holding fast or seeking protection from evil through God; ʿiṣma may mean protection from attackers or subtle help that keeps someone from sin.
rows.anchor: والاعتصام: الامتناع، واعتصم فلان بالله: إذا امتنع من الشر به، والعصمة من الله: دفع الشر عن عبده

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abu Ali and Abu Hashim hold that divine protection means either preserving a servant from plots or giving subtle aid that lets the servant avoid sins.
rows.anchor: والعصمة من الله على وجهين: أحدهما: بمعنى الحفظ، فيمنع كيد الكائدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view explains divine ʿiṣma as command and guidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الأمر والدلالة، يقال: عصمه، فلم يعتصم من الناس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The pronoun in به may refer to the proof, understood as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الهاء في قوله: به قيل: يعود على البرهان، وهو القرآن، عن ابن جريج وأبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the pronoun refer to God's name: believers hold fast to God to seek His pleasure.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعود على اسم الله على معنى الاعتصام لطلب مرضاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative صراطا is analyzed either as the direct object, because the verb implies making them know a path, or as a circumstantial phrase meaning guidance to truth; the author prefers the latter.
rows.anchor: وفي (صراط) قولان: أحدهما: على المفعول به؛ لأن فيه معنى يعرفهم صراطا مستقيما

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali b. Isa attributes the circumstantial analysis of صراطا to meaning-based syntax.
rows.anchor: فحمل النصب على المعنى، وهو على هذا الوجه حال عندنا، عن علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Maida is Medinan by consensus; verse counts differ by region, with the Kufi count judged most sound because it is the count of the Commander of the Faithful.
rows.anchor: هي مدنية بالإجماع، وهي مائة وعشرون آية في الكوفي، وثلاث وعشرون في البصري

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited Surat al-Maida in his Farewell Pilgrimage sermon and called it the last surah revealed, instructing listeners to follow its lawful and forbidden rules.
rows.anchor: وروي أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قرأها في خطبته في حجة الوداع، وقال: هي آخر سورة نزلت من القرآن

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb reports the Prophet promised ten good deeds for every breath of each Jew and Christian, ten sins erased, and ten degrees raised for reciting the surah.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: من قرأ سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says the surah is entirely decisive and unabrogated except the ban on those heading to the Sacred House, which consensus says was abrogated by later commands.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم: وكلها محكمة، لا نسخ فيها، إلا قوله: (ولا آمين البيت الحرام) فإنهم أجمعوا على نسخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author affirms abrogation of the inheritance oath passage despite disagreement about it.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (فيقسمان بالله) وفيه خلاف غير أنا أثبتنا نسخها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has حرم with a damma; Yahya b. Yaʿmur reads it with a sukun. Both are plural forms of حرام.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة حرم بضم الراء، وعن يحيى بن يعمر (حرم) بجزم الراء سكنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of حرم denotes what is forbidden, and a person in consecration is named for refraining from perfume, clothing, and hunting that were normally lawful.
rows.anchor: وهما جميعا جمع حرام يقال: رجل حرام، وقوم حرم، وحرم، وحرام من الإحرام

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim treats الوفاء and الإيفاء as equivalent: fulfilling a commitment is the opposite of treachery.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو مسلم، والوفاء معروف، يقال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines contracts as covenants and calls them the strongest kind, deriving the word from tying and joining things together.
rows.anchor: والعقود: جمع عقد، وهي العهود، قال الزجاج: هي أوكد العهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet compares binding a covenant for a neighbor to tightening a rope's girth and binding its upper tie.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: قوم إذا عقدوا عقدا لجارهم ... شدوا العناج وشدوا فوقه الكربا
